core_obligations: Complete the map a to a distinguished triangle and replace the cone by a K-flat complex with flat terms (proof lines 14590-14593).
Fit the composite into a distinguished triangle whose middle term N is K-flat by the two-out-of-three property (proof lines 14594-14600).
Build the morphism of distinguished triangles from the new triangle to the original one (proof lines 14601-14610).
Conclude that the arrow N to L is a quasi-isomorphism by two out of three, or by applying the triangulated-category lemma in the derived category (proof lines 14611-14620).
In the case where K has flat terms, refine N so that its degree n term is the direct sum of M^n and K^n, which keeps N K-flat with flat terms (proof lines 14621-14627).
proof_roadmap: Replace the cone by a K-flat resolution (proof lines 14590-14593).
Produce a K-flat N mapping to the original triangle (proof lines 14594-14600).
Check that the resulting map to L is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 14601-14620).
Improve N in the flat-terms case (proof lines 14621-14627).
difficulty_reason: The lemma factors a map from a K-flat complex into an arbitrary complex through a K-flat complex, up to homotopy, with the factor map a quasi-isomorphism, and shows that flatness of the terms can be preserved. The proof is a pure exercise in the triangulated structure of the homotopy category: it completes the map to a distinguished triangle, replaces the cone by a K-flat complex with flat terms, uses the triangle axioms to build a new triangle whose third term is K-flat by the two-out-of-three property, maps it to the original triangle, and concludes that the new arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by two out of three. The improvement of the constructed complex to one with flat terms in each degree is obtained from the refinement lemma on distinguished triangles.
